questions.question: In learned medicine, what was the first prescription?
options: Regimen: food, wine, exercise, and sleep
questions.explanation: Regimen (food, wine, exercise, sleep) came first. Celsus spends book after book on what to eat.

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 5:23 advise?
options: Take a little wine for the sake of your stomach
questions.explanation: “Take a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent ailments.” “A little” is the ethical dose.

questions.question: How does the chapter describe honey?
options: Calories, cough syrup, and the best topical antiseptic they owned
A cheap food for the poor only
questions.explanation: Honey was calories, cough syrup, and the best topical antiseptic they owned. It was costly and mixed into bitter roots.

questions.question: How was fruit such as grapes, figs, and pomegranates generally classed?
options: Warming and drying, good for phlegm
Cooling and moistening, hence fever food
questions.explanation: Fruit was generally cooling and moistening, hence fever food. Legumes, by contrast, were warming and drying.

questions.question: What kind of meal matched a “hot” disease?
options: Spices, broths, oil, and diluted wine
Fruit, light grain, less wine, and cool rooms
Nothing at all until the fever broke
questions.explanation: Hot diseases got fruit, light grain, less wine, and cool rooms. Cold diseases got spices, broths, oil, diluted wine, and motion.
